request.description:
Creates a transaction that converts fiat to a digital asset.

Where the converted asset is delivered depends on whether you send `wallet_address`:

- **Include `wallet_address`** — the asset is sent to that address on the network you specify. Use this when each customer holds their own wallet.
- **Omit `wallet_address`** — the asset is credited to your Ramp merchant custodial wallet, and you credit the customer on your own ledger. Use this when you hold balances for your customers.

The `merchant_reference` must be unique. Reusing one returns a duplicate transaction error.

response.status: Transaction successfully initiated.

request.description:
Locks the quote and generates a single-use bank account for the customer's deposit. This request takes no body.

The customer must transfer exactly `amount_expected`, which is the transaction amount plus the processor fee and VAT. Deposits above or below that amount are rejected. The name on the paying account must match the customer name on the transaction, because third-party deposits are not supported.

Note that `data.reference` here is the **bank account** reference (`BANK_ACCOUNT_...`), not the transaction reference. Store it separately — overwriting the `TRX-...` reference from the create response breaks transaction lookups.

Only confirm when the customer is ready to pay.

request.description:
Requests a GHS mobile money debit against an on-ramp transaction you have already created.

The response carries `next_step`, which tells you how the customer authorises the debit:

- `OTP` — the provider sends a one-time code. Collect it and call **Verify a mobile money OTP**.
- `PIN` — the provider pushes a prompt to the customer's handset. They approve it there and you take no further action.

Call this endpoint again to send the customer a new code. There is no cap on resends.

response.status: Mobile money deposit successfully initia

response.name: 400 The deposit could not be initiated.
response.status: The deposit could not be initiated.

response.name: 403 The private key is missing or invalid.
response.status: The private key is missing or invalid.

request.description:
Submits the one-time code the provider sent to the customer. Only call this when `next_step` was `OTP`.

This endpoint is idempotent, so a customer can submit a code more than once for the same transaction without it being charged twice. If the code expires, initiate the deposit again to send a new one.

response.status: Mobile money deposit verified.

request.description:
Creates a **static** NGN bank account tied to one customer. Any fiat sent to it is converted automatically and delivered to the wallet address you registered, with no per-transaction API call.

Use this for recurring funding, where a customer keeps their own account details. For one-off purchases, use the standard on-ramp flow, which issues a single-use account per transaction.

Static accounts are available for NGN on request and require the customer's BVN.
